item.title: AI Governance Is Cloud Governance: From Posture to Proof
CSA STAR for AI Certifications: What are They?
item.description: The CSA STAR for AI program extends STAR, the largest cloud assurance program in the world, to artificial intelligence. Any organization that develops, orchestrates, or delivers AI services can benefit from completing a STAR for AI certification. item.title: The AI Threat Landscape in 2026: What You Need to Know
item.description:
Artificial intelligence is changing cybercrime, but not necessarily by creating new types of attacks. Instead, AI is making familiar threats faster, cheaper, and easier to carry out. Phishing, identity fraud, credential theft, and attacks on software systems can now happen on a much larger scale. They used to require much bigger teams.

item.description:

item.title: Lost in Delegation
item.description:
When AI starts acting on our behalf, fluency is no longer the skill that matters
Since February 2025, the AI Act has obliged organisations to work on their staff’s AI literacy. Since July 2026, after the omnibus, only to “support” it. Europe is softening the duty to train people to use AI just as AI starts acting on its own.

item.title: Human-in-the-Loop: When Should a Human Approve an AI Action?
item.description:
AI can give security teams machine-scale capacity, but it cannot make human accountability disappear. The challenge for AI-first security organizations is deciding which actions agents may take and which need human approval. item.title: The Cloud Configuration Blind Spot: Lessons from GitHub’s Outage
item.description:
Executive Summary: GitHub’s August 17 outage illustrates a difficult truth about modern cloud infrastructure: a configuration can be technically present, correctly formatted, and still fail to protect the system it governs. The real risk emerges in the dependencies between components. In this blog, we examine what this incident reveals about continuous security posture monitoring.

item.description:
